title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement: You get a list of tokens in reverse Polish notation: each operator comes after its two operands. Tokens are integers or one of + - * /. Evaluate the expression. Division cuts the result toward zero. The input is always valid.

example.caption: Read left to right. 2 1 + gives 3. Then 3 3 * gives 9.

idea.sentence: Push numbers on a stack. An operator pops the top two numbers, combines them, and pushes the result back.

jargon.plain: Operators written after their operands. 2 1 + means 2 + 1. No brackets are ever needed.
A number an operator works on.

watch.inputHint: One argument: tokens as strings, e.g. ["2","1","+","3","*"]

compare.bruteLabel: Rescan for the first operator and splice the result in

rows.name: Rewrite the list
rows.note: Find the first operator, replace three tokens by one, repeat. Each rewrite shifts the list.

rows.name: Stack
rows.note: Every token is handled once. The stack holds at most the numbers seen before their operator.

fast.takeaway: The notation is already in evaluation order. A stack holds the numbers that are still waiting for their operator.

stages.title: Setup
stages.note: An empty stack for waiting numbers, and the four operations. Division truncates toward zero.

stages.title: Push numbers
stages.note: A token that is not an operator is a number. Push it.

stages.title: Pop two
stages.note: An operator takes the top two numbers. The top one is the right operand, the one below is the left.

stages.title: Push result
stages.note: Apply the operator to left and right. The answer is a new number, so push it back.

stages.title: Return
stages.note: A valid expression leaves exactly one number. That is the value.

edges.title: One number
edges.why: No operator ever runs. The stack holds the answer.

edges.title: Negative number
edges.why: The token -7 is a number, not the minus operator. Test for an operator by exact match.

edges.title: Truncation
edges.why: 7 / -2 is -3.5. Cut toward zero gives -3. Floor would give -4.

edges.title: Operand order
edges.why: Pop the right side first. Then 3 - 5 is the left minus the right, not the other way round.

gotchas.text: Math.floor rounds -3.5 down to -4. Use Math.trunc to cut toward zero. Dividing with / never gives an integer, so you must truncate yourself.
Math.trunc(-0.5) is -0. It prints as 0 and == 0, but Object.is(-0, 0) is false. Harmless here, but know it exists.
Integer division on ints already truncates toward zero, so -7 / 2 is -3. Do not add a correction, and do not convert to float.
Pop the right operand first. For - and / the order matters: a - b, with a popped second.
Do not detect numbers by checking for a leading digit. -11 starts with a minus sign. Check for the four operator strings instead.

recap.key: Push each number. On an operator pop right then left, apply it, push the result. Division truncates toward zero.
moves: On an operator, pop b then a
The last remaining number is the answer
